shortIntro.title: What Your Device Needs for Smooth Clash of Clans Gameplay
shortIntro.para1: Clash of Clans is one of the most well‑optimized strategy games on mobile — it’s designed to run on a wide range of devices. That said, a stable device with responsive hardware helps prevent lag during massive attacks, slow load times between battles, and delayed UI responses.
shortIntro.para2: Although COC isn’t built for high‑FPS graphics like shooters, having a modern chipset, faster storage, and updated OS gives you snappier animations, quicker troop deployment, and less frustration during Clan Wars and Legends League pushes.

intro: Below are the updated minimum and recommended specs needed to enjoy Clash of Clans without hiccups on Android and iOS, based on official info and community benchmarks from real players.

minimum.GPU: Basic GPU support (Adreno 305 / Mali‑T720 or equivalent)
minimum.Storage: At least 600MB free space (to fit game files + updates)
minimum.Internet: Reliable 2–5 Mbps connection to avoid attack disconnects

recommended.Internet: Low‑latency 4G/5G or stable Wi‑Fi for multiplayer & Clan War performance

fps_intro: Clash of Clans caps internal frame rates differently than FPS shooters, but your device’s refresh rate and GPU power influence UI smoothness and animation fluidity.

fps_list.fps: 60–90 FPS very fluid menus on 90–120Hz screens

faqIntroText: Here are the most common questions about Clash of Clans performance and device support (answered in a friendly, real‑player style):

faqList.question: Can COC run smoothly on old phones?
faqList.answer: Yes — COC is optimized for legacy devices, but you might notice slower menu transitions and longer load times compared to newer phones.

faqList.question: Does Clash of Clans support high refresh rate screens?
faqList.answer: COC doesn’t crank FPS to 120 like shooters, but devices with 90–120Hz displays feel more fluid thanks to faster screen redraws.

faqList.question: Do I need a fast internet connection?
faqList.answer: Speed isn’t everything — low latency (ping) matters most. A stable 3–7 Mbps connection is usually enough for smooth wars.
